args: Tablet and desktop application interface design as disciplines distinct from responsive web design. Narrow scope. TABLET: (1) why a stretched phone layout fails on a tablet and what the named alternatives are — Apple's NavigationSplitView and three-column layouts, Material's canonical layouts (list-detail, supporting pane, feed) and the navigation rail, and the window size class systems both platforms use (Apple size classes, Material window size classes with their breakpoint values in dp); (2) iPadOS multitasking — Split View, Slide Over, Stage Manager, and what a designer must guarantee when the app does not own the full screen; (3) hybrid input — designing for touch and pointer and an external keyboard simultaneously, including iPadOS pointer effects and hover states that must not be load-bearing; (4) the specific numeric breakpoints and layout guidance each platform publishes for large screens, and Google's stated large-screen app quality guidelines. DESKTOP: (5) desktop application design conventions that browser-based design does not cover — menu bar and application menus, window management and resizing behavior, multi-window and document-based apps, keyboard shortcut conventions and where they differ between macOS and Windows, right-click context menus, and drag and drop between windows; (6) what Apple's macOS Human Interface Guidelines and Microsoft's Windows design guidance (Fluent) each require that a web design would omit; (7) Electron and Tauri desktop apps specifically — the named failure of shipping a website in a window, and what a designer must add to make a web-technology app feel native (platform keyboard conventions, window chrome, menu integration, offline behavior). Prioritize primary sources: developer.apple.com Human Interface Guidelines for iPadOS and macOS, m3.material.io adaptive layout guidance, developer.android.com large screen guidelines, and learn.microsoft.com Windows design docs. Reject blog restatements where a primary source exists.
